statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-80229: in libcurl's multi interface with OpenSSL 3 provider configurations, a pooled TLS connection can outlive the easy handle that created it, and the OpenSSL library context attached to that handle is freed while the connection still points to it, leading to a heap use-after-free (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-80229.html). curl lists it as affecting releases from 8.14.0, with 8.17.0 through 8.21.0 affected on the current release line, and fixed it in curl 8.22.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/7ea37abc6ac0120ba5f6d94be8d196f7cf1506bb, which is in the curl-8_22_0 release tag and not in curl-8_21_0. Alpine also lists it as fixed in curl 8.22.0-r0 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-80229). The DHI Alpine curl package is built from Alpine's aports curl recipe at the upstream curl release, and its build definition carries no patch for this CVE. The DHI curl packages for Alpine 3.23 are builds of curl 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0 (in both the main and the security repository), 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, on x86_64 and aarch64, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. None of the builds before 8.22.0-r0 is based on curl 8.22.0 or later, so 8.22.0-r0, the first build of curl 8.22.0, is the first fixed build. Every published DHI Alpine curl build uses OpenSSL 3 with provider support (libcurl links libssl.so.3 and libcrypto.so.3 and imports the OSSL_PROVIDER functions), so the affected code is built in.
